page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mix of average and weak results. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1880.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1892.0. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3944.96 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4435.0. Memory bandwidth performance is also on the lower end, with read-only large block bandwidth at 26.17 GB/sec, though write bandwidth for large blocks remains average at 28.03 GB/sec. The instance excels in single-threaded text processing and gzip compression, scoring in the strong tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i-flex.xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not require sustained high multi-core utilization or massive memory bandwidth. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions provides acceleration for specific cryptographic and vector operations without the cost of dedicated GPU hardware. This makes the instance suitable for web serving, light text processing, and general-purpose applications with bursty or moderate CPU demands.
